explanation: The LORD invites Noah and his household into the ark, identifying Noah as righteous amid his generation.
context: This summons follows the ark's construction and moves the account from preparation to preservation.
application: Respond to God's word with faith and responsible action.

explanation: Noah receives different instructions for clean and unclean animals, with greater numbers of the clean animals.
context: The distinction becomes important when Noah later offers sacrifices after the flood; the text does not explain every detail of the classification here.
application: Pay attention to what Scripture actually commands rather than assuming every instruction is identical.

explanation: Birds are also included in the preservation instructions, with the stated purpose of maintaining life on the earth.
context: The command extends God's concern for living creatures beyond Noah's immediate family.
application: Practice stewardship that considers future generations and the wider creation.

explanation: God specifies seven days before the rain and announces a forty-day period of judgment.
context: The time warning gives Noah a definite interval before the flood begins, while the coming destruction is described plainly.
application: Treat warnings seriously and use available time wisely.

explanation: Noah obeys the LORD's instructions, repeating the testimony of obedience at the end of the preceding chapter.
context: The brief statement links God's command in verses 1–4 to the actions that follow.
application: Let faithful conduct accompany professions of faith.

explanation: The narrative dates the flood to Noah's six-hundredth year, anchoring the event within the book's family chronology.
context: The age notice precedes the entry into the ark and the more precise date in verse 11.
application: Remember that obedience is required throughout the stages of life.

explanation: Noah enters the ark with his wife, sons and daughters-in-law because of the approaching floodwaters.
context: The household's entry fulfils the covenant-related promise given in Genesis 6:18.
application: Value God's provision and act on His instructions.

explanation: Clean and unclean animals, birds and creeping creatures are named among those entering the ark.
context: The verse begins a list completed in verse 9, showing the breadth of animal life included.
application: Recognize the importance of preserving the life God has made.

explanation: Animals enter in male-and-female pairs according to God's command to Noah.
context: The verse completes the animal list and recalls the earlier preservation instructions.
application: Follow clear responsibilities carefully and consistently.

explanation: After the seven-day interval, the floodwaters arrive as God had announced.
context: The narrative records the fulfilment of the warning given in verse 4.
application: Do not confuse delayed consequences with the absence of accountability.

explanation: The flood's beginning is precisely dated and described through waters from below and above.
context: The verse combines a chronological notice with the opening of the deep and the heavens, depicting the overwhelming arrival of the flood.
application: Approach accounts of divine judgment with reverence rather than sensationalism.

explanation: Rain falls for forty days and nights, fulfilling the duration previously announced by God.
context: The verse confirms the warning of verse 4 and precedes the account of the waters increasing.
application: Recognize the seriousness of God's word and promises.

explanation: The eight members of Noah's household are named as entering the ark on the appointed day.
context: This verse supplies the family detail behind the earlier summary of entry in verse 7.
application: Be attentive to the welfare of those entrusted to your care.

explanation: The ark receives land animals and birds according to their kinds, continuing the preservation of created life.
context: The repeated phrase 'after his kind' recalls the categories used in the creation narrative.
application: Care for the created world without neglecting human responsibilities.

explanation: Living creatures enter the ark in pairs, preserving life through the coming flood.
context: The account restates the entry of animals, emphasizing the fulfilment of God's instructions.
application: Value orderly preparation in fulfilling important duties.

explanation: Male and female creatures enter as commanded, and the LORD Himself shuts Noah in.
context: The closing of the ark marks the completion of entry and the transition to the rising floodwaters.
application: Trust God's care while obeying what He has clearly required.

explanation: The floodwaters rise and lift the ark above the ground, so the means of preservation begins to float.
context: This verse introduces the movement of the ark as the forty-day flood develops.
application: Remember that provision and protection may come amid difficult circumstances.

explanation: The waters increase greatly and the ark moves upon their surface.
context: The description continues the rising-water sequence begun in verse 17.
application: Do not mistake surrounding turmoil for proof that God has abandoned His promises.

explanation: The floodwaters reach even the high hills described as being under the whole heaven.
context: The narrative stresses the flood's extraordinary scope; interpretations of its geographic extent differ among readers.
application: Avoid overconfident claims beyond what an interpretation can securely establish.

explanation: The waters rise fifteen cubits and cover the mountains, adding a numerical detail to the preceding description.
context: The measurement is presented as part of the account of the waters' height.
application: Read biblical numerical details attentively and without embellishment.

explanation: The flood brings death to moving land creatures and human beings outside the ark.
context: The verse lists the categories affected, emphasizing the gravity of judgment rather than inviting graphic speculation.
application: Take the moral consequences of wrongdoing seriously.

explanation: The text specifies that land creatures possessing the breath of life die in the flood.
context: This verse elaborates the preceding list by describing those on dry land.
application: Recognize the dependence of creaturely life upon God.

explanation: The narrative summarizes the destruction on the ground and the preservation of Noah and those with him in the ark.
context: The summary contrasts the widespread loss of life with the household and animals kept within the ark.
application: Receive God's mercy with gratitude and humility.

explanation: The waters prevail for one hundred and fifty days, extending the flood chronology beyond the forty days of rainfall.
context: The verse closes the chapter and leads into the account of God's remembrance of Noah in Genesis 8.
application: Persevere patiently when a difficult season lasts longer than expected.
